subject.title: [Bug]: Standalone codex CLI login and gateway 'openai' profile are separate auth stores, and there is no headless way to refresh the gateway one

question: Should OpenClaw retain separate gateway-managed OpenAI profiles and improve recovery guidance, or should it sponsor a supported headless/device authorization flow for gateway profiles?
rationale: The report combines a likely discoverability defect with a new OAuth-recovery capability; choosing credential ownership and supported noninteractive OAuth behavior requires maintainer and upstream-contract judgment.

options.title: Clarify and link existing recovery
options.body: Keep separate stores, explicitly state that standalone Codex relogin does not refresh the gateway profile, and document the supported chat or token-paste recovery route.

options.title: Sponsor device authorization
options.body: Add a provider-owned device-code recovery flow only after confirming the upstream OAuth and Codex runtime contracts permit it safely.

options.title: Unify credential lifecycle
options.body: Design a shared credential lifecycle only if maintainers accept the compatibility, security, and per-agent profile ownership implications.

recommendation.title: Clarify and link existing recovery
recommendation.body: Keep separate stores, explicitly state that standalone Codex relogin does not refresh the gateway profile, and document the supported chat or token-paste recovery route.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter can validate the observed headless gateway workflow, while code-history ownership could not be established in the blocked read-only environment.
